static_traits.name: Lu Kai
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, keeping 3 dogs and 2 cats
static_traits.social_status: Having a supportive group of friends and colleagues, but not yet talking about these specific feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior psychological counseling/treatment history; no similar problems in occupational settings before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic; able to self-reflect and cooperate in exploration; tending to personalize events and interpret them in all-or-nothing terms; nervous emotions and prone to overthinking; speech pace not mentioned.

basic_info.main_problem: When clients miss appointments, I develop feelings of being rejected and insecurity.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent feelings of being rejected and insecurity have affected my work performance and overall physical and mental health, so I hope to get support; I just do not want to always feel this way.
growth_experiences: About six months ago, a long-term client missed an appointment. I immediately assumed she had found a new veterinarian, which became the starting point for the recurring thought and emotion pattern thereafter: whenever a client no-shows, I treat it as dissatisfaction or rejection toward me, then worry about losing clients, doubt my professional competence, and develop anxiety and insecurity.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / incompetent
People will abandon me / leave me
Only others' recognition proves my worth

special_situations.event: A client missing an appointment (not yet arriving or not yet notifying in advance)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a client misses an appointment, it means they are dissatisfied with me and will leave me next.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated self-doubt and excessive caution at work; trying to avoid any mistakes through self-monitoring; meanwhile soothing oneself with rational interpretations like 'the client is busy'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She must have already found a new veterinarian; I am losing another client.

special_situations.event: A single no-show record or last-minute cancellation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One negative event represents the overall trend (one miss = they are generally dissatisfied).
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on negative clues, ignoring evidence that past clients would rebook; when interacting with clients is more tense and cautious.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If they miss just once, it means I am no good and they are leaving.

special_situations.event: Recalling the client missing the appointment when being alone at night
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot guarantee clients arrive on time every time, it means I am not perfect enough, not professional enough.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly rehearsing and self-examining in my mind before sleep; trying to control uncertainty by 'thinking it through'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must have done something wrong; this is all my problem.

special_situations.event: New no-show cases continuing to appear, or seeing not-yet-arrived appointments in the schedule
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: An excellent veterinarian should not be stood up by clients; otherwise it equals failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Judging myself by all-or-nothing standards; more tense at work; avoiding discussion with colleagues to avoid appearing 'unprofessional'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I were really good enough, this would not happen; since it happened, I am not good enough.

special_situations.event: A client absent without any explanation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Their silence is expressing dissatisfaction; silence = negating me.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Speculating about the other person's thoughts internally, yet avoiding checking with colleagues or friends and seeking support.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They must be dissatisfied with me, secretly looking down on me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be stably recognized and chosen by clients, feeling needed and valuable
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected, abandoned, and seen as incompetent, thereby losing relationships and self-worth
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control over relationships through self-monitoring and self-blame; avoiding being abandoned
Lowering anxiety through rationalized interpretation; temporarily suppressing the fear of being rejected
Avoiding exposing vulnerability to peers, to reduce shame and the risk of further negation

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough service provider / a person who could be abandoned at any moment
object_relations.object_representation: Critical, easily-departing clients / people expressing dissatisfaction through absence

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing 'whether to express these feelings to friends/colleagues'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: He tends to think others will not understand him, and may even look down on him (transferentially projecting inner shame and negation expectations onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain a gentle, non-judgmental tone, first empathize with their fear of being misunderstood, then with open questions invite them to recall small fragment evidence of 'being understood', gradually loosening the negative expectations of others.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to examine evidence and challenge the automatic inference that 'the client will leave me'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Converting complex emotions into rational analysis for control (e.g. emphasizing 'the client is busy'), to avoid directly touching the vulnerability and fear of being rejected
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First affirm the value of their rational analysis, then gently bring attention back to the current emotional experience (e.g., bodily feelings and emotion intensity), using short sentences, a slower speech rate, and pauses to help them contact their feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reviewing the event of a client missing an appointment and quickly attributing responsibility to oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing uncertainty and frustration in relationships as self-problems, to maintain a 'sense of controllability' over the situation
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Labeling her self-blame pattern in a supportive, shame-free tone; inviting distinction between facts and inferences; using gentle rhetorical questions to guide her to see situational factors; encouraging first-person feeling statements (e.g. 'I feel...').

manifestations: When facing inner unease and worry about being rejected, hesitating to ask friends and colleagues for help, worrying about 'not being understood'
Interpreting clients' silence or absence as negation of oneself; experiencing estrangement and distance in the relationship
outcomes: Sleep impaired and excessive night-time overthinking
Tense interactions with clients, work affected

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeated self-doubt and excessive caution when interacting with clients; worrying that the slightest slip will bring negation
Personalizing clients' absence; reinforcing harsh self-reproach

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Assuming clients are dissatisfied with oneself or 'will leave'; mind reading without evidence
Worrying friends and colleagues will not understand oneself, thus not asking for help

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to do some behavior toward other people or things, and does it to oneself instead.
manifestations: Having a support system but choosing not to express or ask for help; internalizing pressure and anxiety
Thinking repeatedly alone at night instead of communicating outward

exception_events.target_problem: When clients miss appointments, the client usually treats it as dissatisfaction and rejection toward herself, falling into anxiety and self-denial.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Several times clients missed appointments but then rescheduled and continued treatment, not leaving.
exception_events.reason: Clue: real evidence shows missing an appointment does not equal the end of the relationship; there are multiple reasonable causes unrelated to the client.

positive_force: Having a supportive network of friends and colleagues (though not yet fully utilized)
Able to identify and discuss one's own cognitive patterns; willing to try reality testing and reappraisal
Has had positive evidence of clients rebooking after missing
Clear help-seeking motivation; willing to practice coping strategies
negative_force: Catastrophizing, mind reading, overgeneralization, personalization, and all-or-nothing thinking patterns prominent
Strong self-monitoring and harsh self-reproach; tending to over-internalize responsibility
High sensitivity to being rejected leading to avoiding help-seeking and relationship contraction
Sleep impaired and excessive night-time overthinking; maintaining the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and self-blame immediately appearing when clients miss appointments; asserting the client will leave
antecedent: The booking system shows absence or last-minute cancellation
Learning the client has not yet arrived on time and has not yet explained why
target_behavior.core_reason: Highly sensitive to being rejected and personalizing single events; treating uncertainty as evidence negating self-worth.
target_behavior.function: Trying to gain a sense of control over relationships through self-blame and high vigilance; reducing anxiety from uncertainty.
target_behavior.consequence: Rising anxiety; impaired attention; tense interactions with clients; work performance affected.

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive thinking at night and ruminating over worries about losing clients, leading to difficulty falling asleep and interrupted sleep
antecedent: Being alone, recalling the missed-appointment event before sleep
A client is absent that day or worries the absence will happen again the next day
target_behavior.core_reason: Trying to 'think it through' via repeated rumination to gain certainty, to combat the fear of being rejected.
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and anxiety; gaining a false sense of control in the short term.
target_behavior.consequence: Sleep impaired; next-day stress and anxiety worsened; forming a vicious cycle.

target_behavior.behavior: Choosing not to express or ask for help when facing the support system; digesting pressure alone instead
antecedent: When thinking of sharing the current situation with friends/colleagues
Invited to explore willingness to seek support
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about not being understood or being looked down on; shame-driven avoidance tendency.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential negative evaluation or being rejected; protecting self-esteem.
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet activated; isolation and anxiety maintained; the problem persists.
